item.title: Max Olesker: Making the Cut review – up close and personal account of comic’s religious conversion
item.summary: Pleasance Dome, Edinburgh This show about Olesker’s lengthy journey to becoming an Orthodox Jew in order to marry his partner is both elegant and nuanced ‘I would do anything for love,” Meat Loaf sang, “but I won’t do that.” Max Olesker would, if his solo show Making the Cut – based on his memoir – is any guide. It recounts the comic and writer’s conversion from liberal to Orthodox Judaism, a process required so he can marry his sweetheart – but which, in the meantime, forbids him from so much as touching her for years on end, and forbids much else besides. Secularists may be left reeling. Olesker himself clearly has deeply ambivalent feelings about what he’s gone through. That all makes for a gripping story, of course, that begins when this former half of Max and Ivan meets his dream woman at the Edinburgh fringe. He’s Jewish, she’s Jewish: what’s the problem? It’s that the Olesker family’s loose-fitting and bohemian religious tradition is not considered Jewish by his fiancee’s.
